note: The 180 accompaniment recordings of GuitarSet (Xi, Bittner, Pauwels, Ye & Bello, ISMIR 2018), CC BY 4.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3371780. Time-aligned chords and tempi here are derived from its annotations (the plain chord annotation of each .jams). Audio is NOT committed: run `npx vite-node scripts/guitarset.mjs` to fetch and decode the microphone recordings (~340 MB fetched from the 657 MB archive by HTTP range request, ~460 MB of .f32 on disk) into guitarset/data/. GuitarSet records each excerpt twice — once comping the progression, once improvising a lead line over it — and annotates BOTH takes with the same lead-sheet chords. The 180 solo takes are left out on purpose: a solo is one note at a time, so its annotation names harmony that is nowhere in the audio, and scoring a chord recogniser against it measures whether the recogniser guesses the same chart, not whether it hears what was played. With them in, this corpus said family 67.6 / recall 39.3; the split was comps 81.7 / 64.1 and solos 53.6 / 14.6, and a knob tuned on that average is tuned half on hallucination. Their beat tracks are sound — a tempo study could use them — but chord accuracy cannot.
